title: A quasi-compact immersion whose preimage of a principal open is affine and whose complement piece over V(f) is closed is an affine scheme

statement_spans.label: author lemma environment with its own label lemma-get-affine (no canonical tag in the snapshot tag list); statement at source lines 2986-2991

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: The result also follows from the morphisms get-affine lemma, but a direct proof is given. Put A' = Gamma(V, O_V); then j' : V to Spec(A') is a quasi-compact open immersion by the quasi-affine lemma, and for the image f' of f the preimage (j')^{-1}D(f') = j^{-1}D(f) is affine, while j'(V) intersect V(f') is a subscheme of Spec(A') mapping isomorphically to the closed subscheme j(V) intersect V(f) of Spec(A), hence closed in Spec(A') by the section-immersion lemma. Replacing A by A' one may assume j is an open immersion with A = Gamma(V, O_V). In this case j(V) = Spec(A): otherwise a principal affine open D(g) meets the complement of j(V) and avoids the closed subset j(V) intersect V(f); since j maps j^{-1}D(f) isomorphically onto D(f) (invert-f-affine lemma), D(g) meets V(f); and j^{-1}D(g), a principal open of the affine open j^{-1}D(f), is affine, so the invert-f-affine lemma again identifies D(g) with j^{-1}D(g) inside j^{-1}D(f), forcing D(g) inside D(f), a contradiction. (source lines 2993-3020)

standard_prerequisites.use: One route to the result, acknowledged up front; the direct proof follows.

standard_prerequisites.name: A scheme whose global sections embed it as a quasi-compact open in the spectrum of those sections is quasi-affine (properties chapter, Lemma properties-lemma-quasi-affine, canonical tag 01P9)
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the quasi-compact open immersion j' : V to Spec(A') used to replace A by A' = Gamma(V, O_V).

standard_prerequisites.name: A subscheme of an affine scheme isomorphic to a closed subscheme of another affine scheme via an immersion is closed (schemes chapter, Lemma schemes-lemma-section-immersion, canonical tag 01KT)
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows j'(V) intersect V(f') is closed in Spec(A') because it maps isomorphically to the closed j(V) intersect V(f).

standard_prerequisites.name: If the preimage of D(f) is affine then j maps it isomorphically onto D(f), and conversely an affine open mapping isomorphically onto its image inside an affine open identifies with a principal open there (properties chapter, Lemma properties-lemma-invert-f-affine, canonical tag 01P8)
standard_prerequisites.use: First use: j maps j^{-1}D(f) isomorphically onto D(f), so D(g) meets V(f); second use: D(g) is isomorphic to j^{-1}D(g) inside j^{-1}D(f), forcing D(g) inside D(f) and giving the contradiction.

core_obligations: Reduce to the open immersion case: A' = Gamma(V, O_V), j' : V to Spec(A') quasi-compact open immersion by properties-lemma-quasi-affine; (j')^{-1}D(f') = j^{-1}D(f) is affine by hypothesis on f and its image f'; j'(V) intersect V(f') maps isomorphically to the closed subscheme j(V) intersect V(f) of Spec(A) and is therefore closed in Spec(A') by schemes-lemma-section-immersion; hence replace A by A', where j is an open immersion and A = Gamma(V, O_V) (proof lines 2996-3005). Final step: claim j(V) = Spec(A); if not, choose a principal affine open D(g) meeting the complement of j(V) and avoiding the closed subset j(V) intersect V(f); j maps j^{-1}D(f) isomorphically onto D(f) by properties-lemma-invert-f-affine, so D(g) meets V(f); j^{-1}D(g) is a principal open of the affine open j^{-1}D(f), hence affine, and the same lemma identifies D(g) with j^{-1}D(g) inside j^{-1}D(f), which forces D(g) inside D(f), contradicting that D(g) meets V(f) while avoiding j(V) intersect V(f) (proof lines 3008-3019).
proof_roadmap: Replace A by Gamma(V, O_V): build j', transfer the two hypotheses, and use the section-immersion lemma for closedness (proof lines 2996-3005).
Set up the contradiction: choose D(g) meeting the complement and avoiding j(V) intersect V(f) (proof lines 3008-3010).
Derive D(g) meets V(f) from the isomorphism j^{-1}D(f) onto D(f), then D(g) inside D(f) from affinity of j^{-1}D(g) and the invert-f-affine lemma, and finish (proof lines 3011-3019).
